title: Margin collapsing
learningObjectives: Explain margin collapsing and apply it in a practical page layout.

understand.concept: In normal block flow, vertical margins of certain block boxes can collapse into one gap rather than add together. Adjacent sibling margins, some parent-child margins, and empty block margins can collapse under defined conditions. Horizontal margins do not collapse.
understand.whyItMatters: Collapsing can make measured gaps surprising. Flex and grid items do not collapse their margins with one another as normal block siblings do. Borders, padding, inline content, and formatting contexts can prevent some cases.
understand.analogy: Two vertical gaps can behave like overlapping claims to the same space: in a simple positive adjacent-sibling case, the larger margin determines the gap.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is only a learning aid; actual sizing and layout follow CSS formatting rules.

explain.narrative: In this simple normal-flow case, the adjacent margins collapse to 30px rather than 50px.

examples.explanation: In this simple normal-flow case, the adjacent margins collapse to 30px rather than 50px.
examples.expectedOutput: A rendered example that demonstrates the topic's CSS behaviour.

practise.guidedTask: Create adjacent blocks with 30px bottom and 20px top margins. Put them in a flex container and compare.
practise.independentTask: Build a small component that demonstrates this concept. Test it with longer content and at a narrow viewport.
hints: Change one value at a time.
Inspect computed styles in developer tools.
Check keyboard and touch access when the example has controls.
